claims.text: AlCrFeNiSi powder is suitable as feedstock for L-PBF manufacturing of miniature components.
A build-platform preheating window of approximately 300–500°C is applicable to AlCrFeNiSi L-PBF.
Build-platform preheating reduces the thermal gradient between the melt pool and substrate.
Reducing the thermal gradient moderates the cooling rate.
The moderated thermal history decreases residual thermal stresses.
The moderated thermal history suppresses the formation and propagation of hot cracks and other defects.
Preheating produces a more equiaxed and refined microstructure.
Preheating reduces dislocation density.
Preheating diminishes detrimental liquid-film formation during solidification.
Detrimental liquid films promote hot cracking and residual stress.
Relative to room-temperature L-PBF, preheated AlCrFeNiSi components will have statistically lower residual stresses.
Relative to room-temperature L-PBF, preheated AlCrFeNiSi components will exhibit fewer hot cracks.
Relative to room-temperature L-PBF, preheated AlCrFeNiSi components will exhibit higher tensile strength and ductility.
Preheating reduces overall processing complexity by reducing the need for post-build stress-relief treatments.
Room-temperature L-PBF produces high thermal gradients that cause substantial residual stresses.
Room-temperature L-PBF of this material produces columnar grains, hot cracking, and degraded mechanical properties.
A geometry of approximately 60 mm × 60 mm × 10 mm is representative of the proposed specimens.
The effects of preheating may vary with part geometry, laser parameters, and powder characteristics.
Substrate preheating has been shown in other metallic AM systems to reduce residual stress and improve mechanical outcomes.
The optimal preheating temperature and its effects on AlCrFeNiSi microstructure, performance, surface finish, and secondary-phase formation remain uncertain.
